file.title: Campaign file
file.subtitle: Each campaign is a four-section acceptance form. Sections are worked in order: one does not open until the one before it is stamped.
file.allZonesUsed: Every microzone already has a form
file.emptyLiveTitle: Your first real campaign starts here
file.emptyLiveBody: The live file is empty on purpose. Pick a microzone below and open the form: the campaign starts with its 14 slots empty, and the app tells you what to do at every step.
file.emptyDemoBody: No simulation campaigns left. Open a new one below to practise the whole process again.
file.createConflict: A campaign for {{zone}} already exists this month. Open it from the file, or wait for next month.
file.sizeHint: Pick the microzone first: the floor is set by the post office, not by this field. A carrier walks whole routes, so the smallest possible drop is the ZIP's smallest route.
file.sizeLocked: The size locks as soon as you collect the first slot: that advertiser bought a specific reach.
file.deleteBlocked: Cannot be deleted: money is already collected or the drop is at the printer. Archive it.
file.deleteFailed: Could not delete: the campaign already holds collected money or is at the printer. Archive it instead.
file.sizeHintFloor: A carrier walks whole routes, not single houses. In {{zip}} the smallest route has {{floor}} boxes: that is the smallest possible drop and this field's minimum. The price of all 14 boxes and the print cost come from this number.
file.sizeHintNoFloor: The USPS route list for {{zip}} could not be read, so the real floor is unknown. The system will take whole routes until your target is covered and report how many boxes that really is.
file.sizeHintLoading: Asking the USPS for the routes in {{zip}} to find the smallest possible drop…

form.expertHint: Gates unlocked. Development only; Ctrl+Shift+E to leave.

blocked.curation: Needs the operating floor of {{floor}} paid slots. {{missing}} to go.
blocked.manifest: Needs section 2 stamped: no curated households means no manifest to cut.
blocked.production: Needs section 3 stamped: nothing is mailed before it is printed.
blocked.curationCost: Needs the drop's cost covered. ${{missing}} still to collect.

form.savedTitle: Every change writes itself to SQLite; there is no save button.

payment.title: Payment record · slot {{slot}}
payment.belowList: ${{diff}} below list price. The actual amount is what gets recorded.

production.awaitingBody: The printer has the manifest. When Action Mail confirms the USPS deposit, stamp it here: from that moment every QR scan that arrives is a result of this drop.
production.noScans: No scans yet. The first ones usually land 3 to 7 days after the deposit.
production.renewalNote: {{business}} leads with {{count}} scans. That is the argument for selling them the next drop.

finance.floorMissing: {{missing}} slots short of the floor of {{floor}}

file1.title: This is the file
file1.body: Each line is a campaign: one postcard drop to 5,000 households in a microzone. No work happens here — you only choose which one to open.

file2.title: The app tells you what is next
file2.body: This amber line is the only thing this campaign is waiting on. You never have to decide where to continue: do that, and the app hands you the next instruction.

file3.title: The four boxes
file3.body: Every campaign moves through four sections, always in the same order. Green is sealed. Hatched is still shut, because the one before it is not finished.

file4.title: Red means owed
file4.body: Red always means money not collected or a step blocked. Green means cleared. Color is never decoration here, so you can trust it.

file5.title: To start from scratch
file5.body: Pick a microzone here and open a new form. The campaign starts with its 14 slots empty, and the app will ask you for the first one.

form1.title: One instruction at a time
form1.body: The only thing to do right now is always at the top. If you get lost at any point, read this line and do that.

form2.title: Work happens in the open section
form2.body: Open it and the controls for that step are inside. Nothing you can see outside it is needed yet.

form3.title: Shut ones tell you why
form3.body: A hatched section is not broken and you are not missing a permission: it says what it is waiting for. The moment that happens, it opens on its own.

form4.title: You can leave whenever
form4.body: Everything saves itself the moment you do it. Go back to the file and the campaign stays exactly where you left it.

file1b.title: First: practice or for real?
file1b.body: Simulation comes loaded with campaigns so you can practise without consequences. Live starts empty on purpose: that is where you run your first real campaign, from zero, one step at a time.

file6.title: The file index
file6.body: Everything you have ever opened. ACTIVE is today's work; ARCHIVED is what you moved out of the way without deleting. The list scrolls inside its own frame: with 3 campaigns or 50, this screen is the same height.

file7.title: Archive and delete
file7.body: The first icon files it away: the campaign leaves the list but keeps its slots, money and audience, and comes back whenever you want. The second deletes for real and asks first. Live, it is blocked once money is collected or the drop is at the printer: that is a business record, not clutter.

file8.title: If something is unclear, ask it
file8.body: The assistant knows this system: formulas, postal acronyms, rules, how each thing is done. It answers only from the documentation and shows you where it read it. It runs on your own server, so it costs nothing and nothing leaves the network.

form5.title: Reach governs everything else
form5.body: How many households get the postcard. The price of all 14 slots, the cost of the drop and the curation cut all hang off this number. Type it and everything recalculates; there is no apply button. It freezes the moment you collect on the first slot.

form6.title: Your costs and what to charge
form6.body: Here you enter what the direct mail house quotes: printing, data, presort, finishing, postage. From that and the reach, the system works out what each slot should sell for to leave your margin, and applies it to the ones not yet paid.

form7.title: The 12" × 9" card
form7.body: The 14 slots as they will print. Drag by the handle to swap two ads: the niche and the business travel together, size and price stay with the box. The USPS zone is untouchable: the indicia and the address go there.

form8.title: Ask without leaving the form
form8.body: Lost a formula or an acronym? The assistant is right here and answers from the system's documentation.

mode.label: Application mode
mode.liveHint: Real data. You only see campaigns you opened yourself, business sourcing really queries Yelp and Geoapify, and curation uses the real audience. An empty file is the correct starting point.
mode.demoHint: Practice file. Your own campaigns for rehearsing the whole process without consequences: delete them whenever. The businesses and routes are real — from OpenStreetMap, Yelp and USPS — only the household audience is synthetic.

reach.label: Drop reach
reach.hint: The price of all 14 boxes, the cost of the drop, the curation cut and the manifest all come from this number. Change it while no box has been collected.
reach.previewCurated: The {{count}} households already curated are discarded: they were selected for the old reach, so curation has to run again.
reach.lockedProduction: The reach is fixed: the drop is already at the printer.
reach.conflict: The reach cannot change: slots are already collected, or the drop is at the printer.
reach.lockedPaid_one: The reach is fixed: one slot is already collected, and that advertiser bought this specific reach.
reach.lockedPaid_other: The reach is fixed: {{count}} slots are already collected, and those advertisers bought this specific reach.
reach.invalid: Enter a figure between {{min}} and {{max}} households.
reach.hintFloor: A carrier walks whole routes, not single houses. In {{zip}} the smallest route has {{floor}} boxes: that is the smallest drop possible. Type your target and the system takes whole routes until it is covered, then tells you the real count.
reach.hintNoFloor: The USPS route list for {{zip}} could not be read, so the real floor is unknown. The system will take whole routes until your target is covered and report how many boxes that really is.
reach.hintLoading: Asking the USPS for the routes in {{zip}} to find the smallest possible drop…

costs.title: Operating costs and suggested price
costs.intro: Enter what the direct mail house and the data vendor quote you. From those costs and this drop's {{households}} households, the system works out what each box should sell for. None of this is public: these are your quotes.

listPerPiece.label: Data and household list
listPerPiece.note: Household file licence (Data Axle, InfoUSA or equivalent) plus CASS/NCOA normalization and validation. Data Axle publishes no rates: it is quoted by volume through Salesgenie, so this one is entered by hand. In simulation mode leave it at 0 and use EDDM routes or Census data.

printPerPiece.label: Offset/digital printing
printPerPiece.note: Large-scale printing of the 12" × 9" jumbo on both sides with all 14 slots. Stock and inks included.

variableDataPerPiece.label: Variable-data ink-jet
variableDataPerPiece.note: Addressing, ECRWSS endorsement, indicia, permit and IMB barcode printed piece by piece.

presortPerPiece.label: Presort and sortation
presortPerPiece.note: Sorting by carrier route and walk sequence, which is what earns the discounted rate.

finishingPerPiece.label: Finishing and USPS packaging
finishingPerPiece.note: Cutting, QC, banding, tray labelling and palletizing to USPS spec.

postagePerPiece.label: USPS postage
postagePerPiece.note: Rate per piece. Defaults to $0.260, the published EDDM Retail price for flats up to 3.3 oz. Adjust it if you enter on your own permit or presorted.

setupFee.label: Setup and prepress
setupFee.note: One charge per drop: proofs, plates, variable-data programming.

deliveryFee.label: Delivery to BMEU/SCF
deliveryFee.note: Last mile for the pallets to the USPS entry unit or sectional center.

targetMargin.label: Target margin
targetMargin.note: What share of what you charge should be left as profit once every cost above is paid.

costs.ready: At these costs and a {{margin}}% margin, selling all 14 slots at these prices covers the drop and leaves that margin. Hero and back are weighted differently because they are worth differently.
costs.unquoted: Only postage is loaded. While print, data and finishing sit at 0, the suggested price covers the mail alone: get the mail house quote and type it above.

assistant.title: Operating assistant
assistant.offline: No answer from {{endpoint}}. Start the server or check the network; meanwhile the raw documentation is shown.
assistant.intro: Ask anything about the system: formulas, postal acronyms, rules, how something is done. Answers come only from the documentation, and the passages are shown.
suggestions: How is the suggested price per slot calculated?
What is the operating floor and when is it met?
What do ECRWSS, IMB and presort mean?
What happens if I change the reach after curating the audience?
assistant.placeholder: Type your question… (Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line)
assistant.grounding: Answers come only from the system's documentation. It runs on your own server: nothing leaves the network and no tokens are spent.
assistant.docsIntro: Anything uploaded here becomes part of what the assistant can quote: mail house quotes, contracts, your own notes, USPS rates. Text formats: .md, .txt, .csv, .json, .yml.
assistant.seedLocked: This is the system's own documentation: it is rebuilt on startup. Edit the file in docs/ to change it.

settings.title: Data and cost settings
settings.sourcesIntro: Where the system gets data in this mode. The free ones cost nothing and are enough to practise the whole process; the paid ones are what a real campaign needs. Each says what it gives and what it does not, and can be tested here with 5 records.
settings.marketIntro: Published market rates, gathered on {{date}}. These are not your quotes: they are for budgeting until you have the real ones, and so simulation works with figures of the right order.
settings.applyPresetNote: Overwrites this mode's cost lines. Your real quotes go in section 1 of the form, and they override this.
settings.dataAxleTitle: Data Axle · what is actually public
settings.routesIntro: This replaces buying a consumer list. USPS publishes every carrier route in a ZIP with its official household count and its demographics; the system scores them and takes the best until your reach is covered. A saturation drop is delivered to 'Postal Customer', so no names are needed.
settings.coveredNote: You asked for {{target}} households and the best {{routes}} routes add up to {{covered}}. It does not match exactly on purpose: whole routes are bought, and postage and printing are billed on the real number.
settings.noCensus: Scored on what USPS publishes alone: median income, age and household size per route. The free Census key adds owner occupancy, single-family share, vehicles and home value.
